card: This pull request moves ownership of txindex, txospenderindex, coinstatsindex, and block filter indexes from process-global variables into NodeContext. Secondary indexes previously relied on static globals and a global filter registry, preventing clean node encapsulation and complicating multi-node testing or multiprocess separation. Call sites across RPC, REST, and net_processing are updated to query indexes via NodeContext or a PeerManager callback. The change is an internal refactoring that alters no behavior except key ordering in getindexinfo output.
evidence: PR description: "This removes the remaining process-global index ownership and stores node-owned indexes in NodeContext instead."
problem: Secondary indexes were held in process-global pointers and static maps. This violated node encapsulation, made it harder to isolate node instances in unit tests or multiprocess setups, and forced unrelated components like PeerManager to access global state directly.

risk.why: Mistakes in index lifetime or destruction ordering could cause crashes or use-after-free during node shutdown, or break block filter serving to P2P peers.

scope_notes: Touches 30 files across index, node, net_processing, rpc, rest, and tests, but the changes outside node/context and node/indexes are largely mechanical call-site updates.
summary: Transfers ownership of secondary index instances (txindex, txospenderindex, coinstatsindex, and block filter indexes) from process-global variables into NodeContext. Introduces custom deleters in a new node/indexes module so NodeContext can own index instances without circular header dependencies. Updates RPC, REST, test helpers, and PeerManager (via an options callback) to access index instances through NodeContext.
